questions.q: Calculate the volume occupied by $0.500\ \text{mol}$ of an ideal gas at $1.50\ \text{atm}$ and $25^\circ\text{C}$. (Use $R = 0.0821\ \text{L}\cdot\text{atm}/\text{mol}\cdot\text{K}$)
questions.exam: States of Matter and Gas Laws
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which rearrangement of the Ideal Gas Law allows you to calculate the **density** ($d​$) of a gas?
questions.explain: Density $d = \frac{\text{mass}}{V}$. Since $n = \frac{\text{mass}}{M}$ (molar mass), substituting into $PV=nRT$ gives $PV = \frac{\text{mass}}{M}RT \implies \frac{\text{mass}}{V} = \frac{PM}{RT} \implies d = \frac{PM}{RT}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the pressure exerted by $2.0\ \text{mol}$ of oxygen gas in a $10.0\ \text{L}$ container at $300\ \text{K}$? ($R = 0.0821\ \text{L}\cdot\text{atm}/\text{mol}\cdot\text{K}$)
questions.exam: States of Matter and Gas Laws

questions.q: An unknown gas has a density of $1.96\ \text{g/L}$ at STP ($0^\circ\text{C}, 1\ \text{atm}$). What is the molar mass of the gas?
questions.explain: At STP, 1 mole occupies 22.4 L. Molar Mass $M = \text{density} \times \text{Molar Volume} = 1.96\ \text{g/L} \times 22.4\ \text{L/mol} \approx 43.9\ \text{g/mol}$. The closest value is 44 g/mol ($\\text{CO}_2$).
questions.exam: States of Matter and Gas Laws
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: If the temperature of an ideal gas is doubled and the pressure is halved, what happens to the volume?
questions.explain: From $V = \frac{nRT}{P}$, if $T​$ becomes $2T$ and $P​$ becomes $0.5P$, then $V_{new} = \frac{nR(2T)}{0.5P} = 4 \times \frac{nRT}{P}$. The volume increases by a factor of 4.
questions.exam: States of Matter and Gas Laws
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the value of the Ideal Gas Constant ($R​$) when pressure is in atm, volume in liters, and temperature in Kelvin?
questions.explain: The standard value for $R​$ in these units ($L\cdot\text{atm}/\text{mol}\cdot\text{K}$) is $0.08206$, commonly rounded to $0.0821$.
questions.exam: States of Matter and Gas Laws
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: A student collects experimental data: $P=1.0\ \text{atm}$, $V=2.0\ \text{L}$, $T=300\ \text{K}$, mass of gas $= 2.6\ \text{g}$. What is the approximate molar mass of the gas?
questions.explain: First, calculate moles: $n = \frac{PV}{RT} = \frac{1.0 \times 2.0}{0.0821 \times 300} \approx 0.0812\ \text{mol}$. Then, Molar Mass $M = \frac{\text{mass}}{n} = \frac{2.6\ \text{g}}{0.0812\ \text{mol}} \approx 32.0\ \text{g/mol}$.
questions.exam: States of Matter and Gas Laws
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which variable is NOT present in the Ideal Gas Equation ($PV=nRT$)?
questions.explain: The standard form $PV=nRT$ includes Pressure, Volume, Moles ($n​$), Gas Constant, and Temperature. Density is derived from it but not an explicit variable in the primary equation.

questions.q: Which of the following assumptions is key to the definition of an "Ideal Gas" used in the $PV=nRT$ equation?
options: Particles have no volume and no intermolecular forces.
questions.explain: An ideal gas is theoretical; it assumes particles are point masses (zero volume) and experience no intermolecular attraction or repulsion.

questions.q: A rigid tank contains gas at pressure $P​$. If you release half the moles of gas while maintaining constant temperature, what happens to the pressure?
questions.explain: Based on $PV=nRT$, Pressure is directly proportional to moles ($n​$). If $n​$ is halved (and $V, T$ constant), $P​$ is halved.
